title: Ghinucci (Bishop of Worcester) to Wolsey, 22 July 1527, and Gilino to Francesco II Sforza, 15 Sept 1527 (Cotton Vespasian C IV): 1520s superscript-digit ciphers

steps.what: Tried DECODE (login required), BL digitised manuscripts and Gallica for images.
Fetched full-size DECODE images of R8476, R8589, R8590, R8613, R8572 with the login cookie; no DOC transcriptions on the records.

L&P iv on BHO and St.P. VI/VII on archive.org: R8476 = L&P 2727 printed with decipher in St.P. VI 552; R8589 = L&P 5282 with the Latin decipherment printed; R8590 = L&P 5300; R8613 = L&P 3291 no. 2, a duplicate of 22 July 1527 'undeciphered'.
Transcribed R8589's cipher and aligned it with the L&P 5282 Latin; the decipherer's diagonal strokes mark nulls.
Established the system: consonant-row glyph + superscript syllable digit, bare glyphs single letters, nulls, codes.
Transcribed R8613 in full (814 tokens) from line crops.
Applied the R8589/R8590 key to R8613: Lautrec, Avemaria, dilationem, perpetuam divisionem came out.
Extended the key from R8613's own context and the L&P 3291 summary (conditiones, duraturam, parcendum pro liberatione filiorum, milliones, colloquia ...).
Sub-agent transcribed R8476 (845 tokens) and aligned it with St.P. VI, giving the code words (Regia Majestas, Rex Gallorum, Pontifex, Gallia ...).
R8613 read to 780 of 814 tokens (95.8%) with the merged key; 34 tokens in a few single-occurrence stretches stay open.
Sub-agent transcribed Gilino R8572 (about 3,150 tokens, 9 pages) and its clear passages; the address leaf names Francesco II Sforza, Duke of Milan.
One-token-one-letter homophonic anneal on R8572 with the it-cinquecento 4-gram model: no Italian (-2.9/char, restarts disagree).
Sub-agent scanned the DECODE Sforza key files (ASMi cart. 1591 R5235-R5300, R5301-R5309) and found R5258 ('Cum equite Bilie'), whose barred G/B/D/o syllable rows match R8572's numbers.
R8572 deciphered with R5258 plus context values: 2,872 of 2,989 significant tokens (96.1%) read as sense; LM check -1.52/char.

Opened the DECODE neighbours of R8572 and R8613 by API (R8566-R8579, R8604-R8619) and listed every Ghinucci/Wigorn record; checked R8540, R8558, R8573, R8582, R8607 by eye. Result: all are Lee/Poyntz/Worcester despatches in the English letter cipher; no further letter in the superscript key on DECODE.
Second image pass on R8613 P1 l4 and l6 at full resolution: 'p10 +?' re-read as p+ and ɔ10, 'v3' as y3.
With h = s (as in R8476), u8 = o, Q1 = i and nulls xi14, Z9, ɔ10, Z2: 'Et si pinguiores eis offerret conditiones' and 'nisi hec eos spes nutriret'; R8613 measured at 797 of 814 tokens (97.9%).

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: R8613 had no decipherment; its key was rebuilt from three other letters in the same cipher whose decipherments are in print (St.P. VI 552, L&P iv 5282) or interlined (R8590), then extended from R8613's own context.

parts.label: Ghinucci to Wolsey, 22 July 1527 duplicate (R8613)
parts.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
parts.basis: Worcester key rebuilt from the decipherments of the sibling letters R8476 (St.P. VI 552), R8589 (L&P iv 5282) and R8590 (interlinear) and extended by context; 797 of 814 tokens (97.9%); first decipherment (L&P: 'undeciphered').

parts.label: Gilino to Francesco II Sforza, 15 Sept 1527 (R8572)
parts.method: read after matching with key from external sources
parts.basis: Sforza key DECODE R5258 (ASMi Carteggio Sforzesco cart. 1591 no. 24, filed under the Cavaliere Bilia) matched to the letter and applied; 2,872 of 2,989 significant tokens (96.1%).

outcome.fraction_read_source: R8613: r8613_reading.txt, 814 cipher tokens (r8613_cipher.txt), 17 unread -> 797 (97.9%); R8572: gilino/reading_r8572.txt, 2,989 significant tokens, 9 unread + ~108 in doubtful words -> 2,872 (96.1%); combined 3,669 of 3,803 = 0.965.

gaps.item: R8613 P1 l1: 3 tokens (c; b t7)
R8613 P1 l7 and l11: 1 token each
gaps.detail: one token, nothing fixes a value

gaps.item: R8613 P1 l8: 3 tokens (W14 K h)
gaps.detail: one place, conflicting glyph values between letters

gaps.item: R8613 P2 l7, l13, l16: single tokens (bn, d8, b6)
R8613 P2 l19 and l22: 3 tokens each
Gilino R8572: 9 unread tokens and ~108 tokens in 45 doubtful words
gaps.detail: writer's a/o and i/e confusions and glyphs the image does not separate; no second copy

outcome.notes: R8613 97.9% (17 of 814 tokens open, scattered single occurrences; image pass of 9 Oct settled 'pinguiores eis' and 'spes nutriret'); R8572 96.1% of significant tokens; R8476/R8589/R8590 deciphered at the time and in print, used as key material. Garbino (BnF Clair. 327) is the Ranzo code of catalogue entry 7 (vasto1527), out of scope.

prior.where: R8476, R8589, R8590 deciphered at the time (St.P. VI 552; L&P 5282; interlinear) and in print; R8613 called 'undeciphered' in L&P iv 3291, which summarises the original Vit. B IX 127 in English; Tomokiyo's partial table.

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
